rank.et: Borrowed from Middle Low German rank, ranc, from Old Saxon *rank, from Proto-West Germanic *rank.

s: edge, brink, rim (outer part of something)

alles, was Rang und Namen hat

Ranzen.et: From Middle High German rans (“belly, paunch, satchel”), 15th century thieves' cant. From the same root as Swedish ränsel and Dutch ransel.
